Hi Samir, the dead_stock note says: a SKU that has never shipped is measured from its earliest movement of any type (normally first receipt), so a product that arrived last week is new, not dead. Hope that helps!

Hi Felix! From the design review: the SKU that crosses a threshold belongs to the higher class. A SKU is "A" if the cumulative share BEFORE adding it is still below a_pct, and "B" if that share is below b_pct. Example: values 50/40/10 → A, A, B (second SKU starts at 50%, below 80%, so it's A even though it pushes to 90%).

Hi @nina! From the design review notes: rounding is half-up (100.5 -> 101), same as finance rounds on the stock ledger. Do NOT use round-half-to-even. Keep arithmetic in integers. So test_half_cent expecting 101 is the correct one.

Hi @david, for STOCKFLOW-116 the design review says RCV/SHP/RTN quantities must be strictly positive as written (no expansion to units); zero or negative on those is a data-entry error -> ValueError. So raw count, not expanded. Happy to pair if useful.

Review of cycle_count_variance (approve): Logic looks correct: computes variance = count - system per (sku, location), handles both system-only and count-only entries, skips zero variance, sorts by (location, sku). One minor note: the `counted_locs` set tracks locations only (not (sku, location) pairs), so if two different SKUs share a bin location, the first loop's `s_loc in counted_locs` check could skip a system entry for a SKU that wasn't actually counted at that location. In practice the second loop catches count-only entries, but a system-only SKU at a 'counted' location with no matching count entry would be silently dropped. Consider using a set of (sku, location) tuples for `counted_locs` to be safe. Otherwise good to merge.
